items.title: Awkwafina Had Zero Culinary Skills, But Her New Show Changed That
items.author: Elissa Suh

items.text:
In her pristine Los Angeles kitchen, Nora Lum—the actor, comedian, and rapper better known as Awkwafina—is standing over a stove with two burners and losing the fight with both. Ramen boils on one; Spam violently sizzles over the other. Surveying the spectacle over FaceTime, her nonagenarian grandmother, Powah, cackles and tells her (lovingly) that it looks like shit.

This scene opens Lum’s new show, Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook.

“Food is so important to being Asian,” she announces to the camera. “You can’t talk about being Asian without food being the thread that pulls it all together.” But what if, like the 38-year-old Lum, you can’t even steam an egg?

Family history complicates the answer further. Raised in Forest Hills, NY, the actor has considerable Queens cred (after all, her Comedy Central show was called Awkwafina Is Nora From Queens), but she is also descended from local restaurant royalty.

In 1952 her great-grandfather Jimmy Lum opened the family’s Chinese restaurant in Flushing, one of the first in the neighborhood at the time. “If you lived in New York, not just Queens, at a certain era, almost 10 out of 10 times, you remember Lum’s,” she says. (When I ask some of the food-world old heads I know about it, they respond immediately with memories of the pupu platter, the lobster egg rolls, and the glitzy, neon-lit decor.)

“I’ll cook for a chef any day. With my family, I’ll order out.”

Nora Lum aka Awkwafina, at Bistro Na's in Los Angeles.Photograph by Pat Martin

Lum, who is half Korean, previously explored her mother’s roots on an episode of No Taste Like Home With Antoni Porowski, but she knows little firsthand about her father’s family restaurant, which closed before she was born. “When they talk about it, it’s like they’re talking about a long-lost family member,” she says.

The Apple TV docuseries follows Lum as she meets and cooks with Asian American chefs and restaurateurs. Many of them are like her, restaurant kids who left and eventually found their way back on their own terms. “A lot of their families did not want them to go into the industry. They’re subverting the stereotype in a way,” she says of chefs like Cory Ng and Zhan Chen of NYC's Potluck Club, who help her resurrect Lum’s as a one-night pop-up.

“I always dreamed of being the intrepid restaurant worker,” Lum says. But her family’s attitude toward cooking was less romantic. “Whether it was dishes or cooking, no one trusted me with it. I convinced myself that I’m just not a cook.”

Zigzagging the country changed that, from blowing up a duck at Mister Jiu’s in San Francisco to manning the wok at the Culinary Institute of America in New York to touring Texas barbecue joints with her friend and fellow comedian Jimmy O. Yang. They stopped by Curry Boys BBQ in San Antonio, where traditional Texas brisket is served atop a bowl of green Thai curry, followed by Eaker Barbecue in Fredericksburg for bulgogi sausage. “Seeing Asian people in this environment that’s so Texas, where the two cultures are very different,” broadened her perception of how chefs layer their influences in a way that wasn’t a compromise.

The pleasure of the show is watching Lum encounter new experiences. At a whole-hog barbecue in a Hawaii-set episode, chef Mark Noguchi tells her they’re going to use an imu, an underground pit oven. She lights up, not missing a beat. “Like the bird?”

Her ignorance is played for laughs but is also the source of the show’s unusual tenderness. Lum is game for almost anything, even when she has no idea what is happening. “It’s like one of those school nightmares where you hadn’t completed the class and then you’re just walking in for the test,” she says.

Things go wrong, and Lum is put through the wringer. The show doesn’t spare her discomfort, but what surprised her most was how gentle cooking for chefs turned out to be. “I’ll cook for a chef any day,” she says. “With my family, I’ll order out.”

Lately she’s perfecting her Bolognese and careful not to oversell the show’s resolution. “As much as it was a journey of food and collective Asian culture, it was also self-discovery,” she says, catching herself. “Probably in a narcissistic way—there’s still a question mark as to what it all means.”

items.text:
Thomas Straker’s namesake London hit makes its stateside debut in NYC this weekend. | Thomas Streat/Straker’s

This is Eater’s guide to all the new restaurants, bars, and cafes that have opened this week in October 2026 Throughout the month, we’ll update the list weekly (see: September, August, July, June, May, April, March, February, January). When we’ve been to a place, we will then include a few openings on our heatmaps (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, cocktail bars) to let you know the ones we like. If there’s an opening in your neighborhood that we’ve missed, let us know at ny@eater.com.

October 7

Spotlight

Soho: London chef and internet butter evangelist Thomas Straker takes over the former Lucky Strike, Keith McNally’s now-closed Soho fixture, for his first restaurant outside the U.K. A late-September opening date for Straker’s was pushed back to Saturday, October 10. The New York restaurant centers on an open kitchen surrounded by steel and green stone, leather banquettes, dark wood, and warm lighting. Expect the modern British cooking style with Italian leanings that defines the Notting Hill original that opened in 2022. 59 Grand Street, at West Broadway

And the rest…

Brooklyn Heights: Brooklyn’s charming new Georgian restaurant Bebo, open since late September, pays homage to grandmas everywhere with comfort foods like khachapuri, vibrant dips, and crockets of soup in a cozy space surrounded by fringed lampshades, cottage curtains, and antique plateware. 145 Atlantic Avenue, between Henry and Clinton streets, Brooklyn

Bronx: After 14 years, neighborhood sports bar Triona’s closed its original location after the Chicago Bears game on Monday, September 28, but reopened next door on Friday, October 2, as Triona’s Vintage Sporting Club. The landmarked Scheffel Hall building dating back to the late-1800s was a German beer hall and restaurant and later housed the German-American Athletic Club and Fat Tuesday’s jazz club. Vintage sports memorabilia joins more than 20 screens and an updated Irish-leaning pub menu, with a continued love for the Bears and Michigan Wolverines. 190 Third Avenue, at East 17th Street

Chelsea: A chic taste of Verona landed in New York on Thursday, October 1, with the arrival of Italian wine bar and bistro Bar Lento. Lento, the Italian word for “slow,” features a brick-framed backdrop with a secret garden inside. The warm setup showcases a wine list of whites, bubbles, and pét-nats from Sardinia to Veneto to go along with seasonal plates like bruschetta and fluke ceviche in a citrus tomato vinaigrette. 158 Eighth Avenue, near West18th Street

Chinatown: Something Smells Fishy, a casual Japanese seafood counter that accepts walk-ins only, specializes in customizable kaisendon rice bowls topped with the likes of raw tuna, salmon, fluke, and uni. 95A Elizabeth Street, near Grand Street

Crown Heights: Brooklyn Surf & Soul, a new takeout spot serving seafood and soul food, opened on October 3. It’ll offer shrimp po’ boy sandwiches, whiting sandwiches, shrimp and grits, seafood boils, fried chicken, and more. 602 Nostrand Avenue, near Pacific Street

East Village: Table Mercato, Boston’s cult-favorite Italian sandwich shop that specializes in crispy chicken cutlets shoved between freshly baked focaccia, added its first NYC location in late September. Chef Jen Royle’s popular Sicilian and spicy vodka Parm sandwiches, priced in the mid-$20s a pop, commanded immediate long lines out front (open 11 a.m. until sell-out). There are also house-made chips, onion dip, and rainbow cookies. 214 E. 10th Street, between First and Second avenues

Financial District: Nationwide ramen bar Kyuramen debuted a trio of fast-casual spots on one 9-to-5 strip in NY on Thursday, October 1. Kyuramen Express slings ramen, udon, rice bowls, sushi, onigiri, and appetizers; Bao Dumpling is a Chinese takeout with a knack for dumplings; and Aokō Matcha offers specialty green drinks and desserts. Open daily from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. for dine-in, takeout, and delivery. 40 Gold Street, near Fulton Street

Lincoln Center: Prolific French chef Daniel Boulud returns across from NYC’s cultural hub in a big way on Thursday, October 8, with the opening of Brasserie Boulud — a consolidation of his closed Upper West Side restaurants (Bar Boulud, Boulud Sud, and Épicerie Boulud) into one massive, 10,000-square-foot flagship. The classically French-leaning Brasserie Boulud features the greatest hits from each dearly missed restaurant in one combined menu. Expect seafood towers, French onion soup, steak frites, lobster souffle, and boudin blanc, along with the return of Boulud’s cult-favorite DB Burger. 1900 Broadway, at Lincoln Plaza

Lower East Side: Australia’s popular and prolific Gelato Messina has made its American debut, with the opening of Softville on October 1. Continuing the city’s fancy soft serve moment, Softville will offer it, made using dairy from Ronnybrook Farm in the Hudson Valley, alongside an extensive and rotating menu of sauces and toppings. It also offers loaded sundaes, such as a birthday cake sundae featuring fior di latte soft serve, butter cake, strawberry pudding, “birthday crumble,” strawberry and white chocolate sauce, cream cheese chantilly cream, and sprinkles. A collaboration with Studio Jeremyville, the shop is described as an “art-led concept store,” in which Studio Jeremyville sculptures and other art will be on display. The art studio has worked with Messina since its early days, creating murals for its stores. 137 Orchard Street, between Rivington and Delancey streets

Lower East Side: Brazilian restaurant Iara opened on Friday, October 2, from chef Vitor Mendes, who previously worked at Brooklyn hot spot Theodora. Mendes cites a trip to his home country of Brazil following his father’s death as inspiration for the restaurant. Before it, he told Eater NY, “I thought that my own culture was rice, beans, and barbecue, as a lot of people might think.” At Iara, he’ll employ cassava in many ways: in the crispy cubes of tapioca served with yellowfin tuna and smoked biquinho peppers, in the vinaigrette paired with his hiramasi ceviche, in the fries that accompany his picanha, and more. 205 Allen Street, at East Houston Street

Park Slope: After shuttering his 120-year-old family bakery in Carroll Gardens earlier this spring, James Caputo is back in the baking business with Caputo Bagels, which opened Monday, October 5. The new bagel shop, a collaboration with Miriam owner Rafi Hasid next door, is all about hand-rolled sourdough bagels, open-face and breakfast sandwiches, as well a familiar take on the bake shop’s famed lard bread. 81 Fifth Avenue, near Prospect Place, Brooklyn

Red Hook: All-day diner and bar Vals debuted in Brooklyn at the beginning of October with a menu full of waffles, Denver omelets, blue-plate specials like spaghetti and meatballs, funnel cakes, and milkshakes. Located in the revived Fort Defiance, Vals’ name nods to the nearby Valentino Pier. Nicely priced drinks at the newly expanded bar include draft cocktails, well drinks, beer-shot combos, Negronis, martinis, and more. The new hangout comes from Victoria Viscusi, chef Allie Gassaway, and Laine Pelka, the latter two of which previously worked in the same space before. 347 Van Brunt Street, at Wolcott Street, Brooklyn

Theater District: Diner 24, the Gramercy greasy spoon known for its giant shakes, hot dogs, and burgers served by singing waiters, added a flagship corner location in the heart of Times Square on Wednesday, October 6. Located right under the historical Lambs clubhouse, the new 235-seat Diner 24 that’s open around the clock also hosts hourly performances from actors with Broadway backgrounds from a dedicated 20-foot stage upstairs. “Mamma Mia” and milkshakes, anyone? 1674 Broadway, at 52nd Street

Times Square: Southern food chain Kitchen + Kocktails by Kevin Kelley, which started in Dallas in 2020, opened its first location in New York City. The restaurant, which is the chain’s largest, will serve dishes such as Cajun crab cakes, fried seafood and chicken, smothered steak, jerk lamb chops, and shrimp and grits. The opening continues the restaurant’s national expansion. It also has locations in Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Miami, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C., and will soon be opening in Boston and New Orleans. 7 Times Square, at 7th Avenue and 41st Street

West Village: Camari Mick’s long-awaited Calabash, billed as an Afro-Caribbean bakery and brasserie, opened for daytime service on Friday, October 2. Running from Thursday to Sunday, daytime service will feature Mick’s acclaimed baked goods, including sticky buns, coconut canelés, and beef patty croissants, plus cornbread pancakes with salted maple sabayon. Dinner service begins on October 9 and will be available for a single 6:30 p.m. seating on Friday and Saturday nights via prepaid bookings. It will offer dishes including suya steak frites using plantain fries and asun pasta with goat ragu and pappardelle. There’s no alcohol here, but there are fermented drinks and NA cocktails. 183 Christopher Street, near Weehawken Street

West Village: The team behind Zimmi’s expands next door on Wednesday, October 7, with the debut of a tiny 15-seat wine bar and cafe called Bar à Part. Look for small plates, an extensive wine list, as well as savory and sweet pastries from acclaimed pastry chef Clodagh Manning – the Ireland native who previously worked at London’s now-closed Lyle’s. 72 Bedford Street, at Commerce Street

Williamsburg: A new steakhouse landed in the neighborhood with the opening of Booth’s Extra Fine on October 6. The restaurant comes from the team behind Nobody Told Me; it gets its name from chef Nick Pfannersteil’s grandfather, Booth, a Milwaukee car salesman with a penchant for steak and martinis. The menu will feature the requisite steaks and martinis, plus horseradish burgers, truffle ravioli, pork chops, rum cherry sundaes, and more. A nightly Martini Hour from 4 to 6 p.m. will offer $12 martinis, $5 mini hot dogs, $2 oysters, and half-priced caviar. The location previously housed Mighty Quinn’s BBQ. 62 South 2nd Street, near Wythe Avenue

Upper East Side: Prolific Southern chicken chain Zaxbys made its Manhattan debut on Wednesday, September 30. Along with its breaded chicken “fingerz” and a dozen sauces, the menu includes Buffalo wings and a salad section it calls “zalads.” Atlanta-based Zaxbys, founded in 1990, has more than 1,000 locations across 24 states. Its only other NYC storefront sits in the Bronx. 1267 First Avenue, between 68th and 69th streets

Upper East Side: NoMad cocktail lounge Obvio – home to the New York Times’ “Martini of the Year” – starts a semi-permanent residency at its Upper East Side sibling Casa Cruz on Thursday, October 1. Every Thursday to Saturday night, the second floor of the Beaux-Arts mansion – redesigned with Obvio’s giraffe-patterned calling card – imports Obvio favorites like the Tamarind Mezcalito along with pisco-centric drink debuts like a Marmalade Martini from beverage director Amy Racine. Chef John Fraser’s popular tartare tacos and burger join new caviar cones stuffed with Toro tuna. 36 E. 61st Street, between Park and Madison avenues

Theater District: Diner 24, the Gramercy greasy spoon known for its giant shakes, hot dogs, and burgers served by singing waiters, added a flagship corner location in the heart of Times Square on Wednesday, October 6. Located right under the historical Lambs clubhouse, the new 235-seat Diner 24 that’s open around the clock also hosts hourly performances from actors with Broadway backgrounds from a dedicated 20-foot stage upstairs. “Mamma Mia” and milkshakes, anyone? 1674 Broadway, at 52nd Street

Times Square: Southern food chain Kitchen + Kocktails by Kevin Kelley, which started in Dallas in 2020, opened its first location in New York City. The restaurant, which is the chain’s largest, will serve dishes such as Cajun crab cakes, fried seafood and chicken, smothered steak, jerk lamb chops, and shrimp and grits. Running from Thursday to Sunday, daytime service will feature Mick’s acclaimed baked goods, including sticky buns, coconut canelés, and beef patty croissants, plus cornbread pancakes with salted maple sabayon. Dinner service begins on October 9 and will be available for a single 6:30 p.m. seating on Friday and Saturday nights via prepaid bookings. It will offer dishes including suya steak frites using plantain fries and asun pasta with goat ragu and pappardelle. There’s no alcohol here, but there are fermented drinks and NA cocktails. 183 Christopher Street, near Weehawken Street

Look for small plates, an extensive wine list, as well as savory and sweet pastries from acclaimed pastry chef Clodagh Manning – the Ireland native who previously worked at London’s now-closed Lyle’s. 72 Bedford Street, at Commerce Street

Williamsburg: A new steakhouse landed in the neighborhood with the opening of Booth’s Extra Fine on October 6. The restaurant comes from the team behind Nobody Told Me; it gets its name from chef Nick Pfannersteil’s grandfather, Booth, a Milwaukee car salesman with a penchant for steak and martinis. The menu will feature the requisite steaks and martinis, plus horseradish burgers, truffle ravioli, pork chops, rum cherry sundaes, and more. A nightly Martini Hour from 4 to 6 p.m. will offer $12 martinis, $5 mini hot dogs, $2 oysters, and half-priced caviar. The location previously housed Mighty Quinn’s BBQ. 62 South 2nd Street, near Wythe Avenue

Along with its breaded chicken “fingerz” and a dozen sauces, the menu includes Buffalo wings and a salad section it calls “zalads.” Atlanta-based Zaxbys, founded in 1990, has more than 1,000 locations across 24 states. Its only other NYC storefront sits in the Bronx. 1267 First Avenue, between 68th and 69th streets

Every Thursday to Saturday night, the second floor of the Beaux-Arts mansion – redesigned with Obvio’s giraffe-patterned calling card – imports Obvio favorites like the Tamarind Mezcalito along with pisco-centric drink debuts like a Marmalade Martini from beverage director Amy Racine. Chef John Fraser’s popular tartare tacos and burger join new caviar cones stuffed with Toro tuna. 36 E. 61st Street, between Park and Madison avenues

Welcome to the Eater Cocktail Heatmap, focusing on the hottest new bar openings in New York every month.

Eater editors do thorough reporting on the most exciting restaurant openings to hit the city, as well as smaller openings worth having on the radar. In this monthly map, we narrow the field to cocktail bars that are drawing the most excitement, buzz, crowds, and early positive chatter, focusing on spots that have only been open for six months or less. When an Eater editor has already been to a place, we share insider tips on what to expect and what’s worth ordering as well.

New to the list in October: We’ve added Japanese cocktail bar Don’t Be Shy in Hudson Square; massive Chinese-leaning cocktail bar/restaurant/karaoke lounge Rewind in Long Island City; South Asian speakeasy Jam & Jaggery in the East Village; and retro bars FKA in the East Village and Velvet Cowboy on the Upper West Side. For now, we’ve removed Bar Chimera, Peek Inn, and Hidden Rivers Beer Garden.

For related drinking guides, check out Eater NY’s picks for the best cocktail bars, dive bars, and wine bars. And for more New York dining recommendations, check out the new hotspots in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens. In need of an insider’s perspective on how to eat well, no matter where you are in NYC? Pick up our book: The Eater Guide to New York City.

The Jacob’s Pickles team turned its space on the Upper West Side (which relocated to Columbus Avenue) into Velvet Cowboy, a new 1970s Southwestern cocktail bar, in September. Find $5 bar snacks, like a take on the McRib sandwich, chili-cheese fries, and a huge funnel cake hanging from a stand.

A massive new restaurant-cocktail bar-karaoke lounge, Rewind, opened in Long Island City this September and is co-founded with AYS Hospitality, which runs Mr. Moto’s restaurant portfolio. The drinks menu, developed by beverage director Ken Chen, who had been at Taipei gastropub Indulge Experimental Bistro, took cues from tea, the Chinese zodiac, and the five elements. Tipsy Blossom represents fire signs and bitter elements, made with whisky, shochu, chrysanthemum, pear, hawthorn, licorice root, and goji berry. The food menu includes truffle-mushroom congee, Taiwanese fried chicken, and wagyu donburi. Per the name, people enter the space by pressing a “rewind” button on a retro boombox outside.

The team behind West Village cocktail lounge Dandelion expanded with Keepers, a new neighborhood-leaning bar and pizzeria, in July. Drinks, courtesy of Ricky Dolinsky (formerly of the View), include interesting Negronis such as the Black Forest, a drinkable homage to Ben & Jerry’s Cherry Garcia; spritzes; and frozens. Food-wise, find crispy tavern pies.

Bernie and Herb’s comes from a trio of 169 Bar alums who wanted to do a neighborhood spot that’s affordable and stays open until late. The bar opened in July, housed in the space that had been part of Coffee Shop, the Brazilian late-night icon in the area for 30 years. Look for drinks around $10 and inexpensive bar food like hot dogs, pulled pork sandwiches, and more.

FKA, which stands for “Formerly Known As,” is all about retro vibes since it opened in September in the East Village. Look for dollar East Coast oysters; dishes like lamb tartare, pimento cheese, Frito pies, and cheeseburgers; activities like pinball and Big Buck Hunter; and drinks like strawberry daiquiris, natural wines, and $8 beer-and-shot combos.

Chef Aarthi Sampath debuted a new speakeasy underneath her East Village restaurant Drāvida in September. Jam & Jaggery takes on the same South Asian foundation, with drinks like the Dirty Currytini with olive vermouth and curry leaves, and the Gola Chaat with shochu, yogurt, pomegranate, tamarind, herbs, and aloo bhujia, the latter of which is a spiced boiled potato snack. Sampath is offering some of her upstairs snacks, along with an Indian-ish burger.

The team, whose bar history includes Bar Valentina and Employees Only, took over the former Bandits space with a French-leaning bar. Bar Etienne opened in the West Village in August, with a very banana-y rum cocktail along with tomato martinis, chocolate Negronis, and wines. The bistro food menu includes steak au poivre and French onion-grilled cheeses, plus desserts created in collaboration with nearby Claude Bakery, such as tarte tatin and that chocolate cake.

New Hudson Square cocktail bar Don’t Be Shy is meant to evoke Tokyo’s stylish Ginza district since it opened in September. Head bartender Shinya Yamao, who worked at now-closed Piora and Tribeca sake bar Shigure, developed a Japanese cocktail menu with a special Trip to Japan menu available only at the nine-seat bar counter, exploring Japanese history and regionality, like the Edo, made with a potato-miso-flavored vodka and a sweet potato-Campari ice cube. Other drinks are available at the table seats, such as the Miyajima, which has momo nigori sake, red shiso, and lemon. Food includes wagyu and egg salad sandos and umami burrata with taro chips, pecans, dashi, and tomato sorbet.

Alas, Enid’s isn’t coming back, but the Greenpoint Fish & Lobster team turned its Greenpoint address into a new bar paying tribute to another shuttered neighborhood fixture. They opened Matches (a nod to Bar Matchless) in August, with $16 cocktails, along with burgers and steak frites.

Co-owners and couple Mercury Tin and Philip Dizard opened Tin’s on the Lower East Side as their ode to their life experiences. It’s a two-floor, New York-meets-Shanghai bar and restaurant that opened in July (and thankfully, the kitchen is fully open, serving those Shanghai-style dumplings). Drinks pay homage to those blending influences; see: an ode to the Dead Rabbit’s Irish coffee with a Shanghai dirty coffee twist.

A new cocktail bar devoted to all things rum opened in Williamsburg in April in the former original Gertie space. Echo Lake offers $12 daily daiquiris and a lager/rum shot combo cutely called Tiny and a Tot, plus seafood-centric plates like oysters with tepache mignonette and green coconut curry chowder. The new bar comes from beverage power couple Chloe Frechette (the former executive editor at Eater sibling site Punch) and Paul McGee, who cut his teeth at Chicago’s now-closed tropical bar Lost Lake. The duo is also featuring their own collection of liquid loot within the intimate basement rum bar, Undercurrent.

The team behind Mexican fine-dining restaurant Corima and burrito hot spot Vato opened a new bar in downtown Manhattan this April. Bar Chucho, a comparatively casual bar counterpart to Corima, offers fantastic drinks like the Desert Rain with sotol, along with lots of micheladas and familiar food like the carne asada-esque burger.

New Williamsburg bar Dokidoki, which opened in July, is just a fun meshing of Latin and Japanese cultures, courtesy of co-owners and cocktail vets A-K Hada, an alum of Please Don’t Tell and Existing Conditions; and Christian Suzuki-Orellana, a semifinalist on Netflix’s Drink Masters. With just a beer and wine license, they’re whipping up fun martinis and honeydew “margaritas” made with shochu, sakes, and local meads. The Japanese-Puerto Rican-Salvadoran bar snacks include a katsu sandwich made with cod on shokupan bread. It’s a small yet cozy space.

Brooklyn cocktail bar Grand Army alums Patty Dennison and Ally Marrone opened their own bar in Williamsburg in May, taking over what was the Ensenada space. The press release describes Kinda Nice as a mix of “late-night diner culture” and “dive bar spontaneity,” which translates to savory and sweet cocktails like the guava Negroni with malted milk and pisco; the Greek Salad martini with Tomato Crop vodka and a piparra brine; and a tequila drink with lime sherbet and a choice of blueberry or strawberry amaro and tequila. The duo also debuted their downstairs dive bar at the address, Shenanigans, with beers, highballs, boilermakers, and DJs (dancing is encouraged)

New Bushwick bar the Museum Bar + Gift Shop is meant to feel like a hella fun natural history museum, which opened in June. The space is covered in illuminated fossils, crystals, and dinosaur heads. The drinks list continues that thread, with the Insectarium, a Negroni-ish drink with insects; and the Ocean Life made with rum, coconut, limes, Curaçao, and cuttlefish ink. The on-site Gift Shop bar focuses on lower-ABV drinks with cafe touches, such as spritzes and milk punches.

Billy Durney was inspired by “one crazy night in Paris many years ago” to open this Brooklyn cocktail bar next door to his Red Hook Tavern, with “reinvented disco-era cocktails,” in May. That translates to vibrant Blue Hawaiians, Adam’s Appletinis, and creamy White Russians and Brandy Alexanders. And yes, there’s an iteration of that famous cheeseburger, too.

This new Gowanus spot, which opened in July, aims to fill the bar gap left by the address’s previous tenant, Dirty Precious, now with a 1980s look. Co-owners Robin Daily and Mike Brown met at Royal Palms Shuffleboard Club, where one worked and the other frequented, respectively. At Shania’s Max Bet, they’re serving up martinis, Midori sours, and beer-shot combos.

It’s a horse girl’s world: Co-founders and couple Elana Shvalbe and Michael Furac opened this new daytime cafe and evening bar in Red Hook in August, with a pony-loving aesthetic. Find gin martinis; a rye-and-rum Old Fashioned with peanut butter and bananas; and a High Life pony-shot combo for $10, along with an Eastern European-ish food menu including pelmeni and cured and smoked fish.

items.text:
政策定位跃升、版号供给趋稳、AI降本加速落地，三重逻辑共振之下，A股游戏板块迎来一轮集中爆发。


10月14日，游戏板块直线大涨，富春股份封上20CM涨停板，宝通科技、凯撒文化、电魂网络相继拉升涨停，盛天网络、大晟文化等个股涨幅均超5%。就在前一天，天娱数科已率先涨停，拉升信号早有预兆。

据澎湃新闻，近日，国家新闻出版署正式印发《出版业发展“十五五”规划》（以下简称《出版业规划》），网络游戏首次被系统性纳入国家级出版业五年规划框架。《规划》明确了加强网络文学、网络游戏监管，引导规范其健康发展，推出一批新大众文艺精品。网络游戏由此被纳入出版业内容生产与传播的总体框架，监管逻辑的变化随之展开。


对于估值已跌至历史底部的游戏板块而言，多重利好同步落地意味着股价弹性被显著放大。Wind数据显示，截至9月初，申万二级游戏行业市盈率已跌至22.50倍，估值分位数仅有12.55%，A股及港股主流游戏龙头2026年市盈率普遍处于11至13倍的历史底部区间。

政策定性升级，行业预期重塑

真正触动市场神经的，是一系列规划文件带来的定性变化。


据澎湃新闻报道，今年3月，《中华人民共和国国民经济和社会发展第十五个五年规划纲要》正式发布，明确提出"推动优质网络文学、网络游戏、影视动漫、精品展览等出海"，并将"引导规范网络游戏健康发展"列为政策目标。与"十四五"相比，"网络游戏"的提及频次从一次增至两次，且分别落在"构建更有效力的国际传播体系"与"健全文化产业体系和市场体系"两大战略维度。


随后出台的《出版业发展"十五五"规划》进一步细化：明确加强版号供给、优化网络出版服务许可证配置，对网络游戏开展精品遴选推荐，并明确提出"推动网络游戏等深耕国际市场，打造具有世界影响的品牌产品"。


这一系列政策信号，将游戏行业从"受管控的内容领域"重新定性为"有文化属性的出版产业"，行业长期政策预期由此获得了更为清晰的锚点。

版号趋稳：供给端确定性打开业绩兑现空间

政策暖风之外，版号发放节奏的持续稳定，为游戏公司的产品管线提供了现实支撑。


9月底，国家新闻出版署公布当月游戏版号审批信息，209款版号一次性下发，其中国产网络游戏206款、进口游戏3款，连续第二个月单月数量突破200款。当前月均百余款的发放节奏已维持相当长一段时间，合规达标的产品拿到版号的概率大幅提升。


供给端的确定性，是游戏公司业绩兑现的第一块多米诺骨牌。当版号不再是悬在厂商头顶的高压线，行业竞争的门槛就从"能不能上线"转向了"能不能做好"。产品储备充足、双端研发能力强、出海渠道成熟的头部厂商，正在借此拉开与尾部公司的差距。


与此同时，基本面数据也提供了支撑。2026年三季度，国内游戏市场实现高单位数增长，出海业务更维持双位数增速。

AI赋能：降本增效正在规模化落地

在版号与政策之外，AI对游戏产业链的渗透，正成为这轮行情的第三重驱动力，也是市场对游戏板块重新定价的深层逻辑。


催化剂之一来自硬件侧。英伟达DLSS5更新，3D神经渲染性能提升2倍，大幅降低了AI实时渲染成本。在新的硬件支持下，AI可自动生成游戏素材、关卡与剧情，游戏研发周期有望大幅压缩，AI的角色正从辅助素材生产，逐步向完整游戏生成延伸。


产业落地层面，头部公司已初步验证规模化降本的可行性。腾讯的全链路AI创作解决方案VISVISE已应用于近100个游戏项目，生产效率最高可提升8倍；三七互娱在发行环节AI辅助生成的2D美术素材占比超过80%，单季度产出超过50万张。


9月以来上游AI模型持续降价，头部模型公司纷纷推出低价套餐，AI应用企业的边际成本随之下降，商业化盈利门槛降低。上游降本与下游需求增长的共振，正是吸引资金持续抱团AI应用赛道的底层逻辑。

items.title: 高盛警告：AI融资暂停撑住了信用债市场，未来两个月或是最后的平静期
items.summary:
海外企业信用债市场正处于一段虚假的宁静之中。高盛警告，当前投资级信用利差之所以保持平稳，并非因为风险消退，而是因为市场上最大的债券发行方——AI科技巨头——暂时停止了融资。这一窗口期或将在未来两个月内关闭。

高盛信用销售交易员Jeffrey Papai在最新报告中表示，自2025年9月起AI相关债券发行骤然停歇，这为市场创造了难得的喘息空间，并为四季度的利差收窄行情提供了技术支撑。他认为当前是买入时机，但明确附加了有效期：一旦AI供给重返市场，这一逻辑即告瓦解。


风险正在逼近，包括博通"APCHIP 2.0"、SpaceX芯片融资以及博通/OpenAI"Jalapeno"项目在内，近期已有约1500亿美元芯片融资进入筹备或发行阶段。


高盛估算，2027年7年期及以内的AI相关投资级债券发行规模将达2750亿美元，占全部短端投资级供给的20%至25%，远高于今年约10%的占比。届时，区域银行、公用事业公司与OpenAI的GPU贷款将同台竞争同一笔保险资金，信用曲线面临显著压力。

利率风暴下，利差纹丝未动

过去六周，利率市场剧烈波动，MOVE指数升破110，美联储加息周期重启，法国主权风险蔓延，而投资级信用利差几乎毫发未损。

历史数据显示，此前两轮加息初期，信用利差均出现明显走阔——2015至2016年周期宽出27个基点，2022年宽出15个基点。而本轮自8月15日至10月15日，利差仅扩大1个基点。与此同时，投资级指数收益率升破6%，为金融危机以来第三次触及这一水平，但利差依然稳定。


资金流向同样展现出韧性。Jackson Hole会议后六周内，投资级基金净流入达120亿美元，处于2020年以来的第65百分位，仅上周单周流入即达50亿美元，远高于今年约30亿美元的周均水平。

企业信用溢价压缩至历史低位

市场平稳的背后，隐藏着另一层隐忧：投资者为持有企业债而要求的额外补偿已压缩至历史最低水平。


Papai指出，上月投资级利差占总收益率的比例首次跌破13%，创下名义值与百分比双重历史低位。对比之下，2008年和2020年市场压力高峰期，这一比例曾超过80%。法国市场同样出现异常——约25%的法国企业债收益率已低于法国国债，市场实际上认为LVMH的信用质量优于法兰西共和国。


Papai将此解读为投资者"对非AI企业整体信用状况日益放心"。但这也意味着，当风险真正到来时，市场的缓冲垫已极为有限。

AI借款人已在指数中"拖累"整体

值得注意的是，Papai在报告中反复使用"非AI"这一限定词，原因在于：AI科技巨头正在成为指数中的隐忧。


将甲骨文、微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta、英伟达、AMD、SuperMicro和博通从投资级指数中剔除后，剩余成分较整体指数窄约2至2.5个基点；而一年前，这一差值约为宽出0.5个基点。与此同时，上述九家公司占指数市值的比例已从不足4%升至逾6%，占指数久期的比例从不足5%升至近8%。


个券层面已有明显信号：博通5年期信用违约互换上周报136个基点，创历史新高；甲骨文同期报261个基点，同样创历史纪录。

供给空窗期制造了虚假平静

Papai直接点明了市场平静的真实原因：目前没有AI相关供给。


统计显示，自2025年9月起，市场进入超过两个月的AI大额债券发行空窗期——这将是AI资本支出建设启动以来，首次出现连续两个月无单笔规模超过30亿美元AI债券发行的情况。回溯2025年9月至今，AI相关30亿美元以上的交易共23笔，合计规模3780亿美元，而9月、10月两月均无新增。


这一规律与高盛AI信用篮子的表现高度吻合：每轮发行潮启动初期对应利差明显走阔，而供给淡季（如5月、9月）则对应信用利差收窄。结合四季度净供给接近零、历史季节性效应以及利率波动率回落等因素，Papai将此描述为"圣诞节利差收窄行情"的技术基础。

然而这段平静即将被打破。


据华尔街日报和英国《金融时报》报道，博通"APCHIP 2.0"Anthropic TPU项目、SpaceX芯片融资、博通/OpenAI"Jalapeno"项目以及甲骨文/英伟达GPU融资近期相继启动，合计规模约达1500亿美元，加上"APCHIP 1.0"尚未完成的逾200亿美元，供给压力已在集结。


更值得关注的是冲击方向的转变。此前AI相关久期供给主要集中在长端TMT板块，而GPU与TPU因折旧周期较短，未来发行将集中在7年期及以内。高盛估算，2027年这部分供给将达2750亿美元，届时区域银行、公用事业公司和工业企业在滚动5年期债券时，将与OpenAI的GPU贷款直接争夺同一批保险资金，预计信用曲线将趋于平坦。


在需求端，目前主要购买者为保险公司。Papai指出，部分保险机构对这类纸面的信心，部分来自于相关公司的股票市值。这意味着，一旦股价出现波动，信贷逻辑的基础将随之动摇。


一旦进入2027年，AI供给机器将携1500亿美元芯片债务重返市场，由信用分析部分依赖发行人股票市值的保险公司承接，而参与安排的银行则拒绝自持。Papai明确表示，这轮行情的有效期是"直到2027年AI供给临近之前"。圣诞节或许会带来利差收窄，但账单将在一月送达。

items.text:
日本国内收益率飙升至数十年高位，正驱动本土金融机构悄然调整资产配置方向。


据英国《金融时报》根据日本证券业协会数据测算，截至今年8月的五个月内，日本大型银行与保险公司合计净买入5.4万亿日元（约340亿美元）、期限两年及以上的日本国债（JGB），创2023年初以来同期最大净买入规模。


与此同时，财务省数据显示，9月份银行对外国债券的净卖出规模升至2.5万亿日元；2026年前九个月，银行外债净卖出总量已超过2005年以来同期任何一年。


这一动向正引发市场高度关注。部分投资者担忧，若资金回流趋势持续扩大，不仅可能推升日元，还可能对美国、欧洲等政府债券市场造成冲击——而这些市场当前正面临数十年来最大的财政赤字压力。

收益率回升，日债重获竞争力

推动上述资产配置转变的核心驱动力，在于市场对日本利率长期维持正值的预期日益稳固。日本央行政策利率目前已升至31年来最高水平，30年期国债收益率今年早些时候一度创下4.27%的历史纪录，10年期国债收益率本月亦触及30年高位。

"日本国债收益率已回升至允许国内投资者将资金留在本土、而非追逐海外回报的水平，"大和资本市场欧洲公司研究主管Chris Scicluna表示。


道富投资管理高级固定收益策略师Masahiko Loo指出，"日本央行更具可信度的货币政策正常化进程，有助于巩固市场对JGB收益率将在较高水平趋稳的预期。"他同时表示，"日本国债正成为全球资本竞争中的有力竞争者。"


此外，日元汇率对冲成本上升，也进一步削弱了日本投资者持有外国债券的实际收益，使本土资产的吸引力相对提升。

外债卖出加速，美债净投资转负

资金回流的信号不仅体现在日债买入端。据日本央行数据，日本对美国长期国债的净投资组合投资今年已转为负值，净卖出规模为2022年以来最高。与此同时，美国和法国债券市场的剧烈波动，也被认为是促使日本银行加速削减外国债券敞口的因素之一。


"历史上，美国和包括法国在内的欧洲经济体是日本债券投资者海外寻收益的主要受益方，"Chris Scicluna表示，"随着日本央行进一步正常化货币政策，这一支撑可能在这些债券市场最需要它的时候宣告终结。"


分析人士指出，在高收益国内资产日益具有吸引力的背景下，日本在海外债券市场的边际影响力不容小觑，尤其是在主要发达经济体预计将录得2021年以来最大财政赤字的当下。

全面回流尚早，市场争议持续

尽管上述动向值得关注，多位分析师仍对"大规模资金回流"的判断持审慎态度。


兴业银行利率策略师Stephen Spratt表示，从数据来看，日本银行削减外国债券敞口的趋势明确，但其购买日债的力度尚未形成令人信服的上升态势。他援引日本央行数据指出，今年8月大型银行贷款同比增长7.9%，显示信贷扩张仍是银行分配资本的更优选项。


养老金资金的动向则更为保守。据英国《金融时报》基于财务省数据测算，今年迄今养老基金对外国长期债券的净买入规模仍高达11.4万亿日元，并无明显撤离迹象。分析师认为，养老基金当前买卖结构的变化，更多是对近期市场行情的机械性再平衡，而非根本性资产重配。


德意志银行东京首席策略师Shoki Omori表示，日本投资者同期增持德国及其他欧洲国债，显示其逻辑更接近"寻找更安全资产"，而非系统性资金回流。"我认为现在断言资金回流已经发生还为时过早，"他说，"我需要看到寿险公司明确卖出外国政府债券的证据，而目前数据还远远不够。"

这一动向正引发市场高度关注。部分投资者担忧，若资金回流趋势持续扩大，不仅可能推升日元，还可能对美国、欧洲等政府债券市场造成冲击——而这些市场当前正面临数十年来最大的财政赤字压力。
收益率回升，日债重获竞争力
推动上述资产配置转变的核心驱动力，在于市场对日本利率长期维持正值的预期日益稳固。日本央行政策利率目前已升至31年来最高水平，30年期国债收益率今年早些时候一度创下4.27%的历史纪录，10年期国债收益率本月亦触及30年高位。
"日本国债收益率已回升至允许国内投资者将资金留在本土、而非追逐海外回报的水平，"大和资本市场欧洲公司研究主管Chris Scicluna表示。
道富投资管理高级固定收益策略师Masahiko Loo指出，"日本央行更具可信度的货币政策正常化进程，有助于巩固市场对JGB收益率将在较高水平趋稳的预期。"他同时表示，"日本国债正成为全球资本竞争中的有力竞争者。"
此外，日元汇率对冲成本上升，也进一步削弱了日本投资者持有外国债券的实际收益，使本土资产的吸引力相对提升。
外债卖出加速，美债净投资转负
资金回流的信号不仅体现在日债买入端。据日本央行数据，日本对美国长期国债的净投资组合投资今年已转为负值，净卖出规模为2022年以来最高。与此同时，美国和法国债券市场的剧烈波动，也被认为是促使日本银行加速削减外国债券敞口的因素之一。
"历史上，美国和包括法国在内的欧洲经济体是日本债券投资者海外寻收益的主要受益方，"Chris Scicluna表示，"随着日本央行进一步正常化货币政策，这一支撑可能在这些债券市场最需要它的时候宣告终结。"
分析人士指出，在高收益国内资产日益具有吸引力的背景下，日本在海外债券市场的边际影响力不容小觑，尤其是在主要发达经济体预计将录得2021年以来最大财政赤字的当下。
全面回流尚早，市场争议持续
尽管上述动向值得关注，多位分析师仍对"大规模资金回流"的判断持审慎态度。
兴业银行利率策略师Stephen Spratt表示，从数据来看，日本银行削减外国债券敞口的趋势明确，但其购买日债的力度尚未形成令人信服的上升态势。他援引日本央行数据指出，今年8月大型银行贷款同比增长7.9%，显示信贷扩张仍是银行分配资本的更优选项。

德意志银行东京首席策略师Shoki Omori表示，日本投资者同期增持德国及其他欧洲国债，显示其逻辑更接近"寻找更安全资产"，而非系统性资金回流。"我认为现在断言资金回流已经发生还为时过早，"他说，"我需要看到寿险公司明确卖出外国政府债券的证据，而目前数据还远远不够。"

items.text:
亚太股市周三从连续两日的跌势中企稳回升，科技与半导体板块领涨，此前纽约联储主席John Williams释放鸽派信号，提振市场情绪。


周三MSCI亚太股票指数上涨0.2%，韩国综指冲高回落；日经225指数高开涨约0.5%。澳大利亚S&P/ASX 200则下跌近1%，表现相对偏弱。

Williams表示，他认为2027年无需进一步收紧货币政策，但仍视今年再加息一次为合适之举。这一表态缓和了市场对加息预期的担忧，令亚洲科技股获得喘息空间。


与此同时，美债收益率维持高位，油价延续涨势，投资者目光聚焦于当日稍晚公布的美国9月CPI数据。


据道琼斯调查，经济学家预测通胀率同比将升至3.6%，高于前值3.4%。油价持续高位运行、汽油价格攀升，为通胀前景增添不确定性，也是当前市场的核心关切之一。

亚太股市反弹，科技与芯片股领涨

Williams的讲话打破了前两日笼罩市场的悲观气氛。MSCI亚太科技股率先反弹，带动整体指数走高。


华尔街见闻提及，周二，享有FOMC永久投票权、被称为美联储“三把手”的纽约联储主席约翰·威廉姆斯（John Williams）明确释放长期的“鸽派”信号。威廉姆斯表示：

我尚未改变可能适合再加息一次的观点。我不认为在此时我有任何理由相信在那之后我们需要做得更多。

当被问及远期（如2027年）的加息路径时，他认为在那时进一步加息是没有必要的。eToro亚太区首席分析师Josh Gilbert表示：

美联储加息次数减少的预期为亚洲股市今日提供了喘息空间。Williams淡化延长紧缩周期的言论令收益率压力有所释放，这对亚洲科技股而言是利好消息。

周三MSCI亚太指数上涨0.2%，从周二触及的8月以来低点小幅反弹。韩国综指一度涨超2%，随后涨幅收窄不足0.5%。此前韩国综指已经连续五日下挫。

韩国芯片巨头SK海力士和三星电子早盘均一度涨逾3%，随后双双回落。

日股市场科技与工业制造板块迎来强劲反攻。日经225指数高开高走，涨幅扩大至0.53%。


AI与半导体产业链成为全场焦点。MLCC巨头太阳诱电大涨7.32%领涨AI硬件板块。受益于数据中心光通信建设需求的藤仓紧随其后，涨3.71%。同时，作为全球科技与AI投资风向标的软银集团亦表现活跃，涨逾2%。

上游高端材料与化工板块同样表现靓丽。半导体封装材料与精细化工龙头力森诺科控股（+3.23%）、住友化学（+2.98%）、德山（+2.30%）以及三井化学（+1.95%）全线上扬。


整体来看，亚太时段上涨呈现出明显的“AI硬件+电子元器件+关键半导体材料”多点开花的板块联动效应，市场风险偏好显着回升，科技成长与周期材料股共同构成了今日盘面的核心支撑力。

油价延续涨势，债市收益率高位企稳

大宗商品与债市方面，原油价格继续走高。


周三亚太时段，WTI原油涨逾1%，至每桶约95.22美元，连续第五个交易日收涨；布伦特原油同样上涨超1%。中东局势持续紧张，能源航运前景不确定性上升，被视为支撑油价的主要因素。

美国汽油零售均价目前约为每加仑4.34美元，较一年前的3.08美元大幅攀升。尽管特朗普上周宣布暂时放宽俄罗斯柴油出口限制，但分析师普遍认为此举对降低燃油价格的实际作用有限。


债市方面，10年期美国国债期货收益率维持在5.21%，较周二小幅上行0.5个基点；澳大利亚10年期国债收益率上行4个基点至5.33%；日本10年期国债收益率小幅上升至3.015%。

汇市整体平静。彭博美元指数基本持平；欧元维持在1.1203美元附近；日元报158.39兑1美元；离岸人民币报6.6940兑1美元。

黄金微跌0.04%，现货价格在每盎司4160美元下方窄幅波动。

items.title: Russia arrests Japanese journalist on spying charges
items.summary: Russian authorities have arrested a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage, accusing him of gathering information related to Moscow's defence
items.text:
Russian authorities have arrested a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage, accusing him of gathering information related to Moscow's defence capabilities for Tokyo.

The journalist, identified as Yuki Imai from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, was detained in the far-eastern Sakhalin region, a day before he was due to leave Russia. He was flown to Moscow where a court ordered he be placed in pre-trial detention, Russian reports say.

Japan says it is still seeking details about the arrest, and has not been able to contact Imai.

The arrest comes as tensions worsen between the two nations after Russian leader Vladimir Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands, claimed by both countries, in August.

Russian authorities allege that Imai "acted on the instructions of [Japan's] national intelligence service" to gather information about people involved in a special military operation on the Kuril Islands, state news agency TASS reported.

The Kuril islands sit between Hokkaido in northern Japan and Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. The archipelago is administered by Russia, but four of the southernmost islands are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.

Russia's FSB security agency published footage showing three masked men in black uniforms storming a hotel room and handcuffing a man. The video then shows him being accompanied onto a plane before appearing in a cage in a Moscow court. It did not say when he was detained or when the court hearing took place.

Imai will be remanded until 12 December, before his trial begins, according to Interfax, another Russian news agency.

Those convicted of espionage in Russia can be sentenced to up to 20 years in prison.

"Tokyo's attempts to use its correspondents in Russia, who hold foreign journalist status, to gather information aimed at undermining our country's security are regrettable," Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said in a statement on Tuesday.

"We cannot help but point out that today's incident is not an isolated one," she noted, but did not name other journalists or media outlets that are allegedly involved in similar activity.

Japan has not commented at length on the arrest. Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told a press briefing that Japan did not know about the arrest until the announcement and had had no contact yet with the journalist.

Imai's published work has covered Russia's relations with North Korea and life in Sakhalin.

Hokkaido Shimbun ran a report on the arrest without naming the reporter. "We are still confirming the details. Ensuring the reporter's safety is our top priority," it said in response to the BBC's queries.

Russia and Japan have been locked in a dispute over the Kurils for decades, and it is the main reason Moscow and Tokyo did not sign a peace treaty after World War Two.

Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sharply criticised Putin's visit – his first-ever to the islands – saying it "wounded the feelings of the Japanese people" and is "incompatible with Japan's consistent position on the Northern Territories".

Moscow dismissed her remarks as "politically inappropriate" and "legally unfounded".

Over the years, attempts to resolve the territorial dispute have made little progress. Bilateral ties have also remained frosty, with Japan imposing sanctions against Russia for its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Last week, Moscow again angered Tokyo by requesting the extradition of the president of the International Criminal Court (ICC), who is Japanese.

The president Tomoko Akane, along with other ICC officials, has been placed on Russia's wanted list since 2023 after the court issued an arrest warrant for Putin over war crimes in Ukraine.

In 2023, Russia detained The Wall Street Journal's Evan Gershkovich on espionage charges and later sentenced him to 16 years in prison.

Gershkovich, a US citizen, was released in a 2024 prisoner swap, the largest exchange since the Cold War ended in 1991.

In 2019, Moscow detained an unnamed Japanese journalist from Kyodo News on suspicion of attempting to obtain military secrets. The journalist, who was picked up in Vladivostok, was ordered to leave the country within 72 hours.

Moscow dismissed her remarks as "politically inappropriate" and "legally unfounded".

Over the years, attempts to resolve the territorial dispute have made little progress. Bilateral ties have also remained frosty, with Japan imposing sanctions against Russia for its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Last week, Moscow again angered Tokyo by requesting the extradition of the president of the International Criminal Court (ICC), who is Japanese.
The president Tomoko Akane, along with other ICC officials, has been placed on Russia's wanted list since 2023 after the court issued an arrest warrant for Putin over war crimes in Ukraine.
In 2023, Russia detained The Wall Street Journal's Evan Gershkovich on espionage charges and later sentenced him to 16 years in prison.
Gershkovich, a US citizen, was released in a 2024 prisoner swap, the largest exchange since the Cold War ended in 1991.

In 2019, Moscow detained an unnamed Japanese journalist from Kyodo News on suspicion of attempting to obtain military secrets. The journalist, who was picked up in Vladivostok, was ordered to leave the country within 72 hours.

Warning: This story includes distressing content

A man has died after falling from a rollercoaster at a Six Flags amusement park on Monday in the US state of Georgia.

The man, Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, was found dead under the ride after being ejected and hitting other people on it, according to police.

An investigation is under way and few details have yet to be released about what happened. Six Flags, the largest amusement park operator in North America, has temporarily closed nine rides across the US and Canada as a precaution.

Here's what we know so far about the incident.

The Cobb County Police Department said the incident at the Six Flags Over Georgia park happened just before 16:00 local time (20:00 GMT) on Monday.

"Officers working at the park responded to an incident involving a male guest on a roller coaster," it said in a statement on Tuesday.

"Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interview indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction."

The ride involved has not been specified but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, and multiple witnesses have identified the ride as the one involved in the incident.

The office of the state's insurance and fire safety commissioner, which enforces amusement park safety rules in Georgia, is also conducting a review.

Officials have not held a news conference on the incident.

The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five.

The company said in a statement that it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident" and that "our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones".

Nick Mendenhall said he witnessed the fatal moments in disbelief, watching the man come out of his seat and then fall into another cart on the ride before falling to the ground.

"It was just super, super bizarre, traumatic. I mean, it took me a couple of seconds, I feel like, to process what was going on," he told the AP. "I cant believe that I just saw that."

He said his mind instantly went to the trauma of all of those impacted by what he witnessed, including the man's loved ones and everyone who was on the ride with him.

One witness told NBC affiliate WXIA that the incident was captured in souvenir photos that were automatically taken of the rollercoaster while it was in motion. The BBC has not been able to verify this statement.

Connor Thompson told the BBC's US partner CBS News that he was in line for the ride when everyone started "yelling, clearly distressed".

"Everyone was kind of confused at first, and then there was someone who was yelling, 'Call 911! Someone fell out!" he said. "At first it was almost like I didn't believe it because I thought that was like impossible for something like that to happen."

He said he saw the cart come into the hub where others were waiting in line and could see the restraint was unlatched.

Another witness, CiCi Nelson, told CNN she, too, was in line to ride the Goliath when the rollercoaster returned and she saw an empty seat with a loose safety bar and a female covered in blood.

Nelson described a scene of hysteria, adding that one man was "freaking out, saying someone fell off".

Brittany Landry, who believed she saw Kariem ejected from the rollercoaster, told Fox News she was in tears.

"I broke because we were just on there," she said.

Kariem's family said he was a father, passionate educator and had survived two bouts of cancer.

His family told WXIA that he had survived cancer twice - the last stint in 2018 - and was in a car crash with his 10-year-old daughter three weeks before his death.

He lived in the nearby city of Atlanta and worked for Wesley International Academy, a public charter school, for more than 12 years as an IT manager, technology teacher and robotics coach.

"Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community," the school said in a statement posted to its Facebook account.

"His love for Wesley, dedication to our students, and commitment to our school community were evident in everything he did."

Outside of work, Kariem enjoyed creating products with his laser engraver and 3D printers, as well as cooking, watching anime and spending time with family and friends, according to his profile on the school's website.

The death at Six Flags Over Georgia is at least the seventh there, according to the Doan Law Firm, which tracks amusement park accidents and represents victims.

According to the firm, this includes two people who had medical emergencies, two who were in restricted areas when they were struck by a ride, two who died in car-related accidents and one who died months after using the park's pool.

Six Flags operates 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico.

In the last 15 years, two deaths caused by falling from the park's rollercoasters led to lawsuits and settlements. One in 2011 involved an Iraq War veteran who was ejected from a ride in New York and hit his head on the car. In the other, in 2013, a woman slipped from her restraints on a rollercoaster in Texas and fell 75 feet.

In September, the Six Flags Magic Mountain park in California announced it was closing its X2 rollercoaster after more 100 people alleged that they had suffered brain injuries from the ride.

With additional reporting by Brandon Drenon

Pull up a party invitation from your calendar, find RSVPs buried in your messages, or play the perfect soundtrack to match the vibe. Siri AI works with your paired iPhone or iPad to find relevant content just for you.

Ask about virtually any topic, from quick dinner recipes to DIY home repairs to game-night trivia. Siri AI taps into broad world knowledge to give you highly specific, up-to-date answers.

Siri AI lets you ask open-ended questions and go back and forth with natural, rich conversations. And your conversations with Siri on HomeView sync to the Siri app on your other Apple devices so you can pick up where you left off.

Heaps of help at home.

Apple HomeView does the heavy lifting when you’re busy around the house. Check your calendar, set reminders, and stay on top of your to-do list. Pull up a quick crafting tutorial. Ask Siri AI to recommend a new coffee shop. Start and stop multiple timers for your chores, and keep an eye on them with Live Activities when you’re using other apps.

Cooking.

When you find a recipe in Safari, just tap the Start Cooking button to view a streamlined format that’s easy to follow.

Handoff.

Start a song, podcast, call, video, or recipe on iPhone, and continue on HomeView without missing a beat.

Apple apps.

A selection of Apple apps are available on HomeView. Enjoy Music with lyrics and artwork, audio stories on News and Audiobooks, and so much more.

Additional apps.

Additional apps.

HomeView supports compatible third-party audio and video apps from your iPhone for a familiar experience across devices.

Astounding sound.

The mighty yet compact speakers pack a serious punch. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. Computational audio adjusts consistency and balance in real time to deliver incredible sound every time, from anywhere. And a down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base — for deep, rich bass.

Spatial Audio.

Fills the room with rich, textured sound for a high-fidelity listening experience.

Multiroom audio.

Use AirPlay to connect with HomePod, Apple TV 4K, and compatible speakers — and just like that, you have a fully connected home sound system.

Friends and family are just a screen away.

Whether you’re calling a friend abroad or calling the kids for dinner, Apple HomeView brings everyone together. Enjoy clear and hands-free FaceTime calls. Use Intercom on HomeView and HomePod speakers to communicate with people throughout the house or on their personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. Send messages and make phone calls using just your voice. And use Find My to help you locate your devices, personal items that have an AirTag, and anybody who chooses to share their location with you.

Center Stage

keeps everyone in the frame during FaceTime calls, even as they move around or if more people join in.

The four-microphone array

picks up voices while reducing background noise, for clear calls and Siri requests.

Everything
connected
and under one roof.

Apple HomeView is a central hub for your smart home accessories, making it easy to keep things running smoothly. And with the new Apple Home Collection, it’s never been simpler to set up and control a connected home.

Integrated with the Home app.

Built into HomeView and synced with your other Apple devices, the Home app keeps you on top of your smart home. See who’s at the door, monitor your entryway, access multiple video feeds, adjust the lighting and temperature, and control scenes and automations to fit the routines and rhythms of your household.

Learn more about the Home app

See it all at a glance.

The Home Modular face gives you a clear and concise look at your home accessories, while the Home Camera face lets you stream up to nine videos at the same time. And you can manage it all with just your voice or a tap.

Enjoy peace of mind.

HomeView can detect the sounds of the smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in your home and alert you on your iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.

Stay caught up.

The Home app uses Apple Intelligence to group related notifications together, such as when a family member arrives home, unlocks the door, and disables the alarm. And with descriptions of video footage, you can use HomeView to catch up on key activity in and around the house.

Multiple users.

HomeView can recognize up to six people and seamlessly switch between them. It syncs with each user’s iPhone or iPad and is designed to show their content only when they’re using HomeView.

Secure Exclaves.

The A18 chip inside HomeView contains Secure Exclaves that process the camera and microphone feeds in a secure compartment that cannot be accessed by the operating system or by Apple. This enables HomeView to recognize the face and voice of each user without exposing the audio and visual data used for recognition to the operating system.

Personal content.

Users can access their personal content on HomeView when their paired iPhone or iPad is connected to the same Wi-Fi network and has been recently unlocked, and HomeView recognizes the person by face.

Expand all
Collapse all

How is HomeView different from other smart displays?

HomeView is deeply integrated within the Apple ecosystem and features a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display and Apple‑engineered audio. Because multiple people can use HomeView, it is designed to keep everyone’s personal information separate.

Users can access their personal content like Messages and Calendar on HomeView when their paired iPhone or iPad is connected to the same Wi-Fi network and has been recently unlocked, and HomeView recognizes the person by face.

The A18 chip inside HomeView contains Secure Exclaves that process the camera and microphone feeds in a secure compartment that cannot be accessed by the operating system or by Apple. This enables HomeView to recognize the face and voice of each user without exposing the audio and visual data to the operating system.

What is the acoustics performance on HomeView?

HomeView delivers room-filling sound with support for Spatial Audio, making it a great way to enjoy music and podcasts at home. Its custom-engineered acoustic system combines a down-firing woofer and two full-range drivers to produce deep bass and crisp highs. Powered by the A18 chip and built-in sensors, computational audio continuously optimizes the loudness and bass response at any volume.

HomeView (Wall Mounted) brings full, balanced sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement, along with support for Spatial Audio.

Where can I buy HomeView?

HomeView will be available on apple.com, in the Apple Store app, and from select partners. You can see it in person at all Apple Store locations. You can also book a session to shop with a Specialist in-store or online. Learn more.
Subject to availability by partner.

Is HomeView an AI device?

HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence. It features Siri AI — a more personal and powerful AI assistant powered by the A18 chip. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri can do even more for each recognized user, like taking action across apps and drawing on personal context to help with everyday tasks.

Can members of my household use HomeView if they do not have an Apple Account or iPhone?

To unlock a full, personalized experience on HomeView, users need an Apple Account, a compatible iPhone or iPad, and to be added as a member of the shared home in the Home app. However, guests and unrecognized users can still easily interact with HomeView to control smart home accessories, check the weather, set timers, and play music — all without accessing anyone’s personal information.

Which smart home accessories work with HomeView?

Thousands of smart home accessories are compatible with HomeView and Apple Home products. Just look for the Works with Apple Home logo. Lights, locks, cameras, and much more are available. You can also automate many tasks and control all your accessories from the Home app on your Apple devices.
